lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: During 2025, sales to our largest two customers were 7.2% and 5.2% of total revenue, respectively.
During 2024, sales to our largest two customers were 8.4% and 6.8% of total revenue, respectively.
All other customers generated less than 5% of sales, and the vast majority generated less than 1% of sales.
During the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, our top ten customers accounted for 35.7% of revenues, and our top customer accounted for 7.2% of revenues.
During the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, our top ten customers accounted for 38.1% of revenues, and our top customer accounted for 8.4% of revenues.
For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, program clients accounted for 83.0% and 83.3% of total revenue, respectively.
For the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company had no major customers to which sales accounted for more than 10% of the Company’s revenues.
The Company had accounts receivable from two customers amounting to 24.1 % of the total accounts receivable balance as of December 31, 2025.
For the year ended December 31, 2024, the Company had no major customer to which sales accounted for more than 10% of the Company’s revenues.
The Company had accounts receivable from two customers amounting to 20.5 % of the total accounts receivable balance.
These statements are inherently uncertain and investors are cautioned not to unduly rely upon these statements.
Costs and fees depend on types of services provided and any special or custom work that we request on behalf of our customers.
To protect our intellectual property, we rely on a combination of laws and regulations, as well as contractual restrictions.

We also rely on the protection of laws regarding unregistered copyrights for certain content we create and trade secret laws to protect our proprietary technology including our e-commerce platform and ERP system.
The Company believes that its redundant network of suppliers provide sufficient capacity to mitigate any dependency risks from a single supplier.
We do not depend on any single supplier.
We rely on the supply of different types of raw materials as well as textiles, including plastic, glass, fabric and metal for our promotional products.

Furthermore, if any of our customers experience a significant downturn in their business, or fail to remain committed to our programs or brands, the customer may reduce or discontinue purchases from us.
We rely on information technology systems to process transactions, communicate with customers, manage our business and process and maintain information.
We rely on software and services from other parties.

We rely on technologies from third parties to operate critical functions of our business, including cloud infrastructure services, payment processing services, certain aspects of distribution center automation and customer relationship management services.

Our success depends upon the continued protection of our intellectual property rights and we may be forced to incur substantial costs to maintain, defend, protect and enforce our intellectual property rights.
We work with multiple raw material suppliers to mitigate lack of availability from a single supplier, however in some cases products with limited numbers of suppliers may become difficult to obtain.

We cannot predict if investors will find our securities less attractive if we elect to rely on these exemptions, or if taking advantage of these exemptions would result in less active trading or more volatility in the price of our securities.

Although we have determined not to avail ourselves of this or other exemptions from Nasdaq requirements that are or may be afforded to smaller reporting companies while our shares and warrants are listed on Nasdaq, in the future we may elect to rely on any or all of these exemptions.

Any future determination to declare dividends will be made at the discretion of our board of directors and will depend on our financial condition, operating results, capital requirements, contractual restrictions, general business conditions and other factors that our board of directors may deem relevant.
As a result, we are permitted to, and intend to, rely on exemptions from certain disclosure requirements.

The Company also relies on the assessment of projected future results of business operations, including uncertainty in future operating results relative to historical results, volatility in the market price of our common stock and its performance over time, variable macroeconomic conditions impacting our ability to forecast future taxable income, and changes in business that may affect the existence and magnitude of future taxable income.

The timing and extent of any purchases depend upon ongoing assessments of the Company’s capital needs, market conditions and the price of the Company’s common stock, and other corporate considerations, as determined by management, and are subject to the restrictions relating to volume, price and timing under applicable laws, including but not limited to, Rule 10b-18 promulgated under the Exchange Act.
